units.text: INT. FAN - CONTINUOUS
No, dear Lord Augustus, you can’t explain anything. It is your chief charm.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Ah! if you find charms in me, Mrs. Erlynne—
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: They converse together .
LORD WINDERMERE moves uneasily about the room watching MRS. ERLYNNE.
To LADY WINDERMERE.
How pale you are!
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: Cowards are always pale!
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: You look faint. Come out on the terrace.
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: Yes.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: To PARKER.
Parker, send my cloak out.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Crossing to her .
Lady Windermere, how beautifully your terrace is illuminated. Reminds me of Prince Doria’s at Rome.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: LADY WINDERMERE bows coldly , and goes off with LORD DARLINGTON.
Oh, how do you do, Mr. Graham?
Isn’t that your aunt, Lady Jedburgh?
I should so much like to know her.
After a moment’s hesitation and embarrassment .
Oh, certainly, if you wish it. Aunt Caroline, allow me to introduce Mrs. Erlynne.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: So pleased to meet you, Lady Jedburgh.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Sits beside her on the sofa .

Your nephew and I are great friends. I am so much interested in his political career. I think he’s sure to be a wonderful success. He thinks like a Tory, and talks like a Radical, and that’s so important nowadays. He’s such a brilliant talker, too. But we all know from whom he inherits that. Lord Allandale was saying to me only yesterday, in the Park, that Mr. Graham talks almost as well as his aunt.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Most kind of you to say these charming things to me!
units.name: LADY JEDBURGH

units.text: MRS. ERLYNNE smiles , and continues conversation .
To CECIL GRAHAM.
Did you introduce Mrs. Erlynne to Lady Jedburgh?
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: Had to, my dear fellow. Couldn’t help it! That woman can make one do anything she wants. How, I don’t know.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Hope to goodness she won’t speak to me!
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: Saunters towards LADY PLYMDALE.
C. To LADY JEDBURGH.
On Thursday? With great pleasure.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Rises , and speaks to LORD WINDERMERE, laughing .
What a bore it is to have to be civil to these old dowagers! But they always insist on it!
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: To MR. DUMBY.
Who is that well-dressed woman talking to Windermere?
units.name: LADY PLYMDALE

units.text: Haven’t got the slightest idea! Looks like an édition de luxe of a wicked French novel, meant specially for the English market.
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: So that is poor Dumby with Lady Plymdale? I hear she is frightfully jealous of him. He doesn’t seem anxious to speak to me to-night. I suppose he is afraid of her. Those straw-coloured women have dreadful tempers. Do you know, I think I’ll dance with you first, Windermere.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: LORD WINDERMERE bites his lip and frowns .
It will make Lord Augustus so jealous! Lord Augustus!
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: LORD AUGUSTUS comes down .
Lord Windermere insists on my dancing with him first, and, as it’s his own house, I can’t well refuse. You know I would much sooner dance with you.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: With a low bow .
I wish I could think so, Mrs. Erlynne.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: You know it far too well. I can fancy a person dancing through life with you and finding it charming.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Placing his hand on his white waistcoat .
Oh, thank you, thank you. You are the most adorable of all ladies!
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: What a nice speech! So simple and so sincere! Just the sort of speech I like. Well, you shall hold my bouquet.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Goes towards ball-room on LORD WINDERMERE’S arm .
